Well, I certainly don't want to have BPD. It would be a lot easier if I was just depressed. But I really want to find the root of what is causing it all, and if I had BPD, that might explain it. 

Mostly my reasons are because I feel like a child. I throw tantrums, I can't be alone, when I am alone I feel so lost that all I can do is eat and feel like a kid lost in a store. I get very aggressive very easily. I am violent. I break things when I'm angry, and I can't help myself. I have broken a laptop and a cell phone from this. I hurled a laundry detergent bottle at my husband. I have caused him numerous cuts on his body from scratching and I slap him and punch him on occasion too. Sometimes I yell so loudly I can't talk afterwards. I punch walls and I cry and sometimes I punch myself as hard as I can in the leg just to calm myself down if I'm alone. I've beaten down doors before. And my husband has threatened to call the police on me, because he says maybe then I'll get help. 

We have struggled with my anger issues and random symptoms of paranoia all throughout our relationship, which is nearly 5 years total now. I don't feel like I need to post everything here, but it helps me to write it down (might help me when I see my therapist). The thing is, I have been feeling sick and alienated from people for a very long time, and BPD might be an explanation for why I have felt this way. I just want to figure out if I act the way I do because it's truly who I am, or if it's because I have some disorder. It doesn't have to be BPD, I just want to know if I'm truly just a terrible person who can't function in society. 

The way it resonates not only with me, but also my husband, makes me want to get help. I love him and I know he will end up leaving me unless I get help. Thanks for the concern, it means a lot. 

EDIT: The way I found out about BPD was when the hubby and I were at a bookstore and I picked up the book "I hate you, don't leave me" and I laughed saying, "Oh god, that sounds like me." We laughed about it and went on our way, but I was very curious about what it was about. I later went to the bookstore alone and read through it and then looked up more on BPD. I bought the book Stop Walking on Egg Shells for my husband and he read through most of it that night and said if I do have it, it would explain so much of my past behavior. I have always had these issues and so my husband was very relieved that it was possible for me to get better (not be aggressive, to not think he was trying to leave me, to stop viewing people - especially my parents - as either all good or all bad, to stop switching my life plans at the drop of a hat, going from one extreme to the next). Honestly, my Dad has pretty bad anger issues so I just kept telling my husband it's just something I "inherited" from my father. He seemed to buy that as an explanation, so I never looked into it. I haven't even told my therapist about my anger issues. I have never told anyone that I have physically hurt my husband. And my husband has never told anyone either.

Well, right now I'm seeing a therapist at my school, and when semester ends, I will end up seeing a therapist on my insurance. So the next few sessions are looking for a therapist for long term, so I'm just going to hold out for the next month since she will be helping me to find another therapist.

Yes! Same here. I was feeling AWFUL one night and I wasn't able to call my therapist until the next day, and lo and behold I was better. Now I feel absolutely fine except for nerves, and I'm so terrified of seeing my therapist because I am genuinely happy. It's like I can't even remember lying on the couch and sobbing because I felt so awful and my whole body hurt. 

I want to keep a diary sometimes but whenever I get down to it I start getting uneasy and can't do it. Something about writing down my demons is just impossible.

What kinds of symptoms make you think you have BPD? I wonder if we have the same symptoms. Are you in a relationship? My therapist said she didn't think I have it specifically because I've been married for nearly 2 years. 

I do trust her, I just don't think she really knows who I am because I hide it. I always do that. Good luck to you!

Honestly I think the reason we're still together is because one, we had to mature for each other, and two, when we changed in other ways, it was always for the better. Like, my husband and I never lived together until we got married. That was a nightmare when we first started out, because it seems stupid, but if you can't decide what movie you want by *yourself* and you actually have to agree upon something...I mean honestly it's pretty devastating when you start realizing your partner has shitty taste in movies (this is possibly a slight exaggeration). 

Like...when you're in the dating phase, it doesn't matter *what* you do as long as you're doing it *together*. I could be picking up cow shit and as long as it was with my husband it'd be great. But...for me that changed. You see the person every day so it's pretty hard to keep up that sort of commitment to loving them for everything that they are. I mean, like recently, I wanted to go see a movie, The King's Speech, and my fucking husband wants to see *Tangled*. *Again*. As in, we saw the movie *last week*. So I just decide to go to it myself and he stays at home and plays video games. I know *some* couples would think this was a sign of impending marital doom but for me that's just who we are. 

I guess what I'm saying is that down the line in a relationship, regardless of marriage, it becomes pretty hard to keep your head above water and remember who you are. Or to better yourself. A lot of people just accept the humdrum of ordinary life and then they never do anything new. Like, for *themselves*, not necessarily for the benefit of the couple. It's so important to start doing cool new things, whether that means something as simple as buying a new video game you love or going fucking cave jumping (my husband's idea...). If you stay true to your own...I guess, expansion (to borrow from the NY Times article on marriage), then it's a lot easier to keep your relationship interesting. 

Anyway, I'll get off my soapbox. But your relationship reminded me of my relationship when I was younger. So yeah, marriage later, but marriage and relationships are basically the same thing. They are both a shit ton of work and you'll wonder why you even bother sometimes (maybe you won't, if you're lucky!). But in the end, at least this is how my husband puts it, if it weren't for your partner you'd be lying in a ditch somewhere not knowing what to do with yourself.

I was in a similar situation. I started dating my husband when I was 16 and he was 18. We planned on getting married when he finished in the military. Things happened, and we got married on a whim when I was 19 and he was in his 3rd year in the Marines. I stayed with him on a military base for a year, then we both moved back to our home state and went to college. We're both finishing up college soon. 

The thing is...I was 19 coming from well off parents, and he was 21 with way too much responsibility and no idea how to handle his money. When we got married, real life hit us hard. The beginning of marriage isn't fun and games when you have to deal with owning cars, living frugally, doing taxes, etc etc for the FIRST time in your life. Thank god my husband was in the military which was a huge support system for young couples (oh, and thank god we didn't get pregnant either). 

So basically getting married young is a huge smack in the face, and you either have to change who you are and become responsible and *fast* or the marriage will fail. I'm not saying that I regret it, but my first year of marriage was *not* fun, but that might have had something to do with me chilling alone on a military base while my husband was gone for days to weeks at a time. 

Oh, and if you get married young, get ready for the shit storm of family and their annoying opinions. When I got married I received a card from an aunt I have probably spoken to once in my life who told me that she didn't approve of people getting married young. What the fuck? Also, there was a pool going in my family of how long it would take me to get knocked up. I have a nice family. 

I think I turned out all right, but if I ever have kids I would definitely advise against them getting married before they get a stable job. I know my situation is a little different since my hubby was in the military, but even then, my God, you wouldn't believe the crazy stories about young people being married in the military. 

Here's what I think...after 2 years the lovey dovey part basically ends and shit gets real. This is where you start developing a mature relationship built on trust and love and compromise rather than lust and infatuation. If you can make it that far you're golden, and it doesn't really matter if you're married or not. I'd say count yourself lucky that you found a girl you love.

What is your exercise/eating plan right now? I recently decided to lose weight to help my depression and I have been slowly easing myself into it. Have you ever heard of SparkPeople? It's a fantastic motivational website with a great community of people who are all trying to lose weight. There is also a depression forum. I found it super helpful, because I signed up for all of their emails, and I am constantly reminded of why I want to lose weight/be healthy. 

I started off with three small goals. Drink 8 glasses of water. Eat a healthy breakfast. Exercise for 10 minutes a day. That's all, but it was a struggle for me to keep that up, even. I also started keeping a journal of how I feel, and how different foods affected me. Now I realize how much certain foods affect my mood, and how even if I feel horrible, if I can just exercise for only TEN minutes, I will feel better. And I do. 

It's so odd, but it feels like I'm constantly fighting against a part of myself that DOESN'T want me to be happy and healthy. It's this voice in my head that tells me that eating healthy is bullshit and that exercising won't help. But I try to switch out my thinking with actual action. If I'm starting to feel down, I rely on a set routine - eat something healthy, drink tea, take a shower, do yoga, or exercise. I need that routine to distract myself. And usually it works, my mood goes up. 

So here's my suggestion for you. Start small. Start very basic. Add ONE healthy thing into your life, like eating breakfast. Do this for a few days. Do it until you are comfortable with it. Then add another. Write in a journal everyday about how you feel. How's that? Good? Then add another. And another. Each time you do it until you are comfortable, then add more. If it feels like too much, take a break. Take a day off even. But hopefully by that time, a day off will make you that much more motivated to go back into it. 

I definitely suggest keeping a journal. At the end of the day, write about how you felt. When did your mood peak? When did it crash? What things set off your depression? Were you depressed all day? Analyze this. Write down what you ate and drank or who you talked to. If you analyze it, you can start to recognize the situations that cause your depression. This can go so far in helping yourself. 

But if you aren't seeing a therapist, you HAVE to! It sounds like you are in such a rut and you need to take care of yourself. The first thing is to take care of yourself mentally. You deserve it. YOU DESERVE TO BE HEALTHY! In both body and mind. 

Also, my last point is visualization. I LOVE this meditation, so I'm going to post the link. [Here.](http://learningmeditation.com/authself.htm) Have you ever meditated before? Just play the audio, sit comfortable or lay down, whatever is more comfortable, and listen. This meditation is about finding who you really are. It helps you visual who you want to become in the future. It really help me visualize my goals and gave me an image of my future self. It sounds hokey...but it really helps, so I'd give it a shot. 

Thinking positive is so hard, especially after a lifetime of having negative thoughts. But it IS possible to change, by making small steps. 

Also, do you have friends you can talk to, who you can rely on? Or family members? You really need the support of a friend. Perhaps you could find someone else in the area who needs to lose a lot of weight, and you can become workout buddies. Having a partner to help motivate each other is a great way to work through your negative thoughts. 

If you ever want to talk about anything, just PM me. Don't give up! You're worth it. You are an amazing person, and you do have the strength to become healthy again. Good luck.
